info.description: The append-only ledger and the served trust snapshots. Six dimensions inside ONE trust system (D53); `computed_through_event` is the last LedgerEvent folded in, which is what makes the S3 replay assertion checkable against a SERVED snapshot rather than against the engine's own opinion.

post.summary: Record one claim-verification outcome and announce it on the ledger.
post.description: The producer of the `claim_verified` event this document already used as its `POST /events` example while declaring no way to emit one. Rows are persisted first and the event appended second, so the ledger never announces a verification the tables do not hold. A replay writes neither and answers 200.

schema.title: ClaimVerificationIn
schema.description:
One verification outcome, as the verifier decided it.

Every field the migration marks NOT NULL without a DEFAULT is required here too, and the
two fields the migration additionally constrains by CHECK — ``status`` and
``provenance_source`` — are validated against the vocabularies that own them. Without
that, a value only Postgres refuses arrives as a 500 from deep inside the writer instead
of a 422 naming the field, which is what a caller can act on.

get.summary: Every store's snapshot, for exchange consumption.
get.description: This is exactly the mapping `validate_bid(..., trust_snapshot=...)` reads. A store with no row here is treated as an UNAVAILABLE eligibility read and denied (R12, fail-closed) — never admitted on the grounds that no blacklist entry was found.

get.summary: What the chain says about every purchase in it. Appends nothing.
get.description: R4's diagnosis door: the pixel and the webhook reconciled with the webhook authoritative, computed and NOT landed. An operator asking "did this purchase grade, and how?" must not have to append to an append-only ledger to find out; `POST /reconcile` is the door for a caller that wants the verdicts recorded. Nothing on this service is authenticated, which is why `limit` is bounded and why the unjoinable-webhook screen runs before the fold rather than after it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many reconciled verdicts to serialise. The fold is never capped; `verdicts_truncated` says whether this bit.

200.description: The fold, computed and not landed.

inputs.description: How many of each LedgerEventKind the fold joined on.

unjoinable_webhooks.description: `order_paid` deliveries naming no order, screened out BEFORE the fold. `POST /events` admits them and the append-only trigger makes the row un-evictable, so they are reported here rather than turned into an outage for every later purchase.

store_aliases_applied.description: Events whose store name was translated from a shop domain onto the platform `store_id` before joining. The two halves of one checkout do not name the store the same way.

post.summary: Reconcile the chain and land the trust update it implies.
post.description: The same fold, appended. The `reconciled` verdicts and the `offer_integrity` observations go onto the hash-chained ledger AND into `ledger.trust_observations` — the table `GET /snapshot` reads — which is R12's "one trust system, not two" taken literally: a transaction outcome moves the same per-dimension Betas a verification outcome moves. Every `event_id` is derived from the order and `event_id` is the ledger's idempotency key, so this is idempotent by construction and safe to run on a schedule, after a delivery, or twice by mistake.

200.description: What was appended, what was already there, and what was written.

appended.description: Events this run added to the chain, by kind.

already_present.description: Events a previous run had already appended. Kept separate from `appended` so "nothing landed" and "nothing to land" are never the same number.

observations_written.description: Rows written into `ledger.trust_observations`. A failed write never fails the fold: the verdicts are already on the chain, so this is a convergence step and re-running converges.

observations_persisted.description: Whether a relational connection was available at all, so a deployment cannot mistake "no connection" for "nothing to write".
